concept.material: mottled verdigris copper and dull olive jade
concept.internal_detail: interlocking brass spur gears and miniature escapement ratchets
concept.button: a domed brass stud set flush into the dorsal seam
concept.button_short: the domed brass stud on the dorsal seam
concept.shell_mechanic: The copper casing splits down the dorsal midline and both curved flank plates pivot outward on side hinges
concept.emerging_parts: A hooked bone beak, two disc-rimmed head plates, and two stout clawed brass feet
concept.signature_move: its olive head plate swivels low toward the surface on a brass ball joint, and its hooked beak clicks open and snaps shut with a dry mechanical clatter
concept.turkish: Kakapo (Yeni Zelanda'ya özgü, uçamayan iri gece papağanı) — kambur oval gövde, benekli bakır pası ve mat zeytin yeşili yeşim taşı

text_to_image: First-person perspective. The protagonist is holding a small mechanical toy in the open palm of one hand. Below the hand is a wooden table that fully covers the background. The toy is small enough to sit comfortably in the palm and is currently in its untransformed state. It is a compact, humped ovate mound-shaped object made of mottled verdigris copper and dull olive jade. The outer shell is completely closed and solid, with fine machined seam lines where the separate fitted panels meet, but no gears, springs or moving parts visible anywhere on its surface. The toy features a domed brass stud set flush into the dorsal seam. Shot on a 50mm macro lens at f/2.8, soft diffused window light from the upper left, shallow depth of field. Natural colour, fine surface texture with faint fingerprints and micro-scratches on the metal.
image_to_video: First-person perspective, filmed in one continuous long take, strictly no cuts or camera transitions allowed. The camera remains steady and does not move. The toy stays in the protagonist's open palm for the entire shot and is never set down. The protagonist's thumb presses the domed brass stud on the dorsal seam briefly and withdraws; this takes under a second and nothing else happens before it. The transformation then begins immediately and fills almost the whole of the remaining shot, unhurried and fully readable from start to finish, never skipping ahead to the finished form. It runs in two stages that never overlap. Stage one: The copper casing splits down the dorsal midline and both curved flank plates pivot outward on side hinges, revealing interlocking brass spur gears and miniature escapement ratchets moving inside. Stage two: A hooked bone beak, two disc-rimmed head plates, and two stout clawed brass feet extend and lock into place one after another, never all at once. Each emerging part appears exactly once and only at its natural anatomical position; nothing is duplicated. Every part carries weight: it accelerates, slows as it reaches its limit, overshoots very slightly and settles back with a small click. Panels slide against each other with visible friction and part along the seam lines already machined into the closed shell. Strictly no parts appear or disappear out of nowhere; every piece was folded inside, and the shell panels stay visible as part of the finished creature. The mechanism is simple and shown clearly rather than elaborate and rushed. After transformation, the final mechanical kakapo's size remains believable and perfectly consistent with what the original toy could realistically unfold into, with absolutely no magical volume expansion. Once fully assembled, the mechanical kakapo performs one short clockwork motion that imitates its species: its olive head plate swivels low toward the surface on a brass ball joint, and its hooked beak clicks open and snaps shut with a dry mechanical clatter. It remains an obviously mechanical toy made of metal, glass and gears at every moment; no skin, feathers, fur, flesh or any organic texture ever appears, and it never turns into a living animal. This motion is brief and takes only about the last two seconds; the transformation itself fills most of the shot. Only in the final second does the finished mechanical kakapo settle into a still pose in the same spot in the palm where the closed toy sat, the lighting unchanged from the first frame, and the shot holds completely steady with no further movement and nothing entering the frame, so the clip cuts back to its opening without a jolt when it loops. Audio: crisp mechanical clicks, servo whirs and ratcheting gears, ending with a soft metallic latch as the transformation completes. No music, no voice.

concept.material: dark walnut burl and brushed gunmetal plating
concept.internal_detail: bronze worm drives and miniature geared rocker arms
concept.button: a flush square gunmetal actuator inlaid with crosshatched knurling
concept.shell_mechanic: The gunmetal upper slab swings upward on a transversal rear pin while the lower walnut casing unfolds sideways
concept.emerging_parts: A blunt chisel-toothed head, two folded jointed forelegs, and a broad cross-hatched paddle tail
concept.signature_move: its flattened tail hinge ratchets upward two notches and strikes down flat against the palm with a dull metal tap
concept.turkish: Kuzey Amerika kunduzu (yassı kuyruklu, kemirgen yarı sucul memeli) — geniş spatula biçimli plaka, koyu ceviz ağacı yumrusu ve fırçalanmış tunç kaplama
